dedupe_keys.name: integrated drought index idi for brazil 2003 2023 cemaden

description: This dataset is a long-term weekly record of the Integrated Drought Index, developed at Cemaden in Brazil to monitor agricultural drought. The Mendeley Data page says the index combines the three-month Standardized Precipitation Index from a 10 km precipitation grid, root zone soil moisture from the GRACE and GRACE-FO satellites (25 km) and the NOAA Vegetation Health Index (about 4 km), released weekly since 2003. It was deposited in 2024 by Marcelo Zeri of Cemaden under the CC BY 4.0 licence, free to download as a single NetCDF file (IDI3.nc, about 30 MB) whose variable IIS3 holds six classes from Exceptional drought to Normal. Coverage is Brazil for 2003 to 2023. Caveats: the page says a publication assessing its accuracy was still being prepared, and the grid resolution of the combined index is not stated on the page read. For simulation it gives weekly drought hazard classes to drive crop loss, hydropower and supply chain scenarios for Brazilian agriculture; Cemaden also uses it in the Monitor de Secas online platform. Related catalogue records include the EDO Combined Drought Indicator for Europe and the Australian Agricultural Drought Indicators evaluation data.
name: Integrated Drought Index (IDI) for Brazil, 2003-2023 (Cemaden)
provider: Marcelo Zeri, National Center for Monitoring and Early Warning of Natural Disasters (Cemaden), via Mendeley Data
